column2: The company that purchased my home equity load which was discharged through bankruptcy six years ago has contacted me and told me that my debt was satisfied through some government program and that they were sending documents to city register to remove the lien from my property. I had to sign some Dodd Frank form and forward it to them. I did that. This was back in the beginning of XXXX. Since then I have checking acris.nyc.gov website to see if the lien was removed but nothing happens. I have contacted the company numerous times and each time they are telling me that the paperwork has been submitted but nothing happens. I went down to the city department that handles the liens and they told me that it takes 5 weeks to process a record. It has been way longer and I am afraid that this is some kind of scam.

This is unacceptable and a huge privacy problem and right now my business partnership is at risk due access to unauthorized information that my partner had access to. \r\nInstitution : Truist Bank XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, FL, XXXX

The Capital One, XXXX, MD. branch representative could not explain how someone took the money but indicated that the debit was through XXXX XXXX XXXX. I pleaded with Capital One to reverse the charge and they seemed to not have been able or unwilling to assist. \r\nAround this time I was leasing one of my properties to XXXX XXXX XXXX ( see attached email ) who admitted that they banked with XXXX XXXX XXXX. I have attached the two affected accounts as well as a line of conversation with the company alleged to have taken the funds. I can be reached on XXXX if you require more information.

In XX/XX/scrub> 2023 my identity was compromised and unauthorized cryptocurrency transactions of about {$8000.00} posted. With added fees/interest the reported balance is now over {$10000.00}. I was a co-borrower on a loan with my son with Wells Fargo. He was 2 weeks behind on his payment. I called the company and told them I was going to make the payment so it wouldn't hurt my credit. They refused the payment and told me I had to pay 2 months or they would not accept anything. I could not afford 2 months and explained it to them. They said that was my problem and I would also have to pay late fees for the 2 months. I told them I would refinance the vehicle. I secured a new loan, and called them with the information. It took a few days past the end of the month to pay it off. They then put a late payment on my credit report. I called them and explained what was going on and they said too bad, not their problem. My credit score was impacted for 7 years till it finally fell off.

Our home flooded during XXXX XXXX. Insurance gave us a {$40000.00} advance, which after many phone calls, CitiMortgage released to us. Our insurance settlement of {$240000.00} was granted in XXXX. Since we had a {$40000.00} advance, we mailed CitiMortgage our check for {$200000.00}. Although we sent the check XXXX weeks earlier, CitiMortgage shows receiving it XX/XX/17. After many phone calls they released {$47000.00} to us on XX/XX/17. I then spoke to XXXX on XXXX who told me the rest of the money would be released and overnighted that week. The check never came so we called back and were told the request \" kept getting bounced back ''. I then spoke to XXXX who explained to me that they are holding {$150000.00} which they refuse to release to us until we are 100 % complete. I have called and spoken to XXXX many times, and they are firm on this because our original contractor 's bid was for much less than it has ended up costing. I have uploaded cancelled ( paid ) checks but they still refuse to release the money, even after we had an inspection showing 90 % complete. We then finished everything structural ( counters, cabinets, etc. ) and had another inspection. That inspection again showed 90 % complete which does not make any sense as all that is left is paint - in fact we are moving home this weekend. I can not make my final payments to the contractor as we have been paying out of pocket all along but CitiMortgage isn't releasing the money, so we are out of money. Today, I spoke to XXXX who again asked for an \" exception '' to release {$100000.00}, but I have asked for this multiple times and never received ( and never received a phone call stating that I wasn't getting it, I keep having to call ). I also asked for another 100 % inspection.

On XX/XX/XXXX I entered into a 13-month CD for {$75000.00} at an interest rate of 4.6 %, which was in line with the market rate at the time. When entering into this CD, I was required to auto-renew to the same maturity ( 13-month ) CD when the original came to term. In JXX/XX/XXXX the CD was auto-renewed at an interest rate of 0.03 %, dramatically below the market rate and the rate the bank was offering to take out a new CD at the same time ( around 5 % ). Then I was charged a break fee of 180 days interest to exit. The bank is exploiting its customers by not allowing them to opt out of auto-renew, then hoping the customer does not break the new CD within the first 6-day period of the renewal, which was done at an interest rate not even close to the rate the bank is offering to new CD customers.

I am submitting this complaint because a debt collector is attempting to collect and report an alleged debt without providing lawful validation as required under the FDCPA ( XXXX U.S.C. XXXX ), Regulation F ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ), the FCRA, and New Jersey state laws, including the NJ Consumer Fraud Act and the NJ Consumer Finance Licensing Act. I formally disputed the alleged debt and requested full validation, including : identification of the original and current creditor, a signed contract or compliant electronic agreement, itemized accounting of all amounts, complete chain of assignment/bills of sale listing my specific account, original statements, proof of charge-off, proof the debt is within the New Jersey statute of limitations , proof of an active NJ debt collection license, and evidence their initial notice met all Regulation F disclosure requirements. The collector has * * not provided legally sufficient verification * *, and instead continues credit reporting and/or collection activity. Reporting and collecting on an unverified debt violates FDCPA XXXX ( b ) and FCRA XXXX ( a ) ( XXXX ), as well as New Jersey laws prohibiting deceptive or unconscionable practices under XXXX. XXXX. Until full validation is provideddirectly from the original creditor, not internal summariesthe collector is required to cease all collection efforts and stop furnishing negative credit information. Failure to do so constitutes continued violations of federal and state law. I am requesting CFPB assistance to : 1. Require the collector to provide full and complete validation ; 2. Ensure they cease collection until validation is supplied ; 3. Correct or remove any unverified credit reporting ; and 4. Ensure compliance with FDCPA, Regulation F, FCRA, and New Jersey statutes.
